about.e1.d: How often the child chooses to wonder.
about.e2.d: How far they push past the first answer.
about.e3.d: Which concepts came up, explained in plain words for parents.
about.e4.d: Persistence: the stone sank, so they tried foam.
about.e5.d: The same question at the start and the end of the session.
about.e6.d: One thing to talk about tonight, plus a try-at-home experiment.
about.l1.d: Draw, say or type anything on the Wonder Board. AI vision reads the drawing and turns it into three real questions.
about.l2.d: Talk out loud to a guide. Every answer ends with a new “but why?”, so each follow-up climbs one rung deeper.
about.l3.d: Test the idea with your hands: drop a stone, wood or foam board in the water and see what floats. Predict first.
about.l4.d: Every question becomes a Journal card, and the same recall question is asked before and after.
about.m1.d: A child’s scribble is input. Vision AI guesses what it is (kindly) and finds the questions inside it.
about.m2.d: Kids ask out loud; guides answer in a real voice with captions. No reading or typing needed to start.
about.m3.d: A 3D world to explore and physics experiments to run. Learning by doing, not by scrolling.
about.m4.d: English, Spanish, Chinese, French, Portuguese, Dutch, Hindi and Tamil, voice and text. 8 is lucky.
about.meas.p: Every number in the parent report comes from what the child actually did in the game, recorded as events. Not from an AI’s opinion, and not a grade.
about.mm.p: Kids scribble, point, talk and build. Curiosity Craft listens to all of it.
about.next.p: Any lesson or picture book becomes a new corner of the island: upload it, and the guides learn its syllabus. Every story a child reads can become a world they can walk into and question.
about.p.lede: Kids ask hundreds of questions a day, until school teaches them that the right answer matters more than the question. Curiosity Craft flips that: it is a world where a child scores by asking “why?”, not by being right.
about.t1: Parents and teachers write the syllabus. Guides answer only from it; anything else gets “that’s not in our island notes yet”.
about.t2: No open web, no search results, no links out for kids.
about.t3: No accounts and no names. Voice is turned into text live and never stored.
about.t4: The game, not the AI, decides when a child climbs the Why Ladder or earns points.
about.trust.h: Built for families and teachers to trust
about.why.p1: Curiosity is the engine of learning. When a child asks their own question, they are ready to remember the answer. Handing them every answer skips that moment.
about.why.p2: Most learning apps reward correct answers. That trains kids to avoid risk. We reward the question, the follow-up and the brave guess, and we make failure funny, so trying again feels like play.
